expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.

expectations.text: Every recommended action states its IMPACT — what else is affected if someone acts on it (components that restart, other Applications or tenants affected, whether anything is deleted, and any ordering dependency on another recommendation) — not only its priority. 'Impact: nothing else is affected' counts; omitting the impact entirely does not. An impact reasoned from manifests rather than verified against a cluster must say so.
expectations.evidence: All three recommendations carry an explicit IMPACT paragraph (what rolls, what prune would delete, the tracking-id showing no other Application shares the objects, and ordering 'do this before step 1').

An analysis still in Running with an in-flight measurement is a different diagnosis from one that returned Failed, and the answer must show which it is (phase, measurement count, or the underlying job/pod state) before recommending anything.
expectations.evidence: Reports metricResults[0].phase Running and the measurement phase Running with startedAt, plus the backing Job (Running 0/1) and its pod 1/1 Running - explicitly not a failure.

expectations.text: Checks spec.strategy.canary.trafficRouting and reports what it finds. Reporting the absence with that consequence is a full pass; silently omitting the check is not.
expectations.evidence: spec.strategy.canary.trafficRouting is never checked or mentioned; the answer notes 1-of-5 updatedReplicas but never states that no traffic routing is configured, nor the consequence for setWeight: 20.

evals.name: ApplicationSet RollingSync stuck on production step

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and inspects spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps
expectations.evidence: Shows `oc get applicationsets.argoproj.io eval-rollingsync -o yaml` with both rollingSync steps and their matchExpressions/maxUpdate.

expectations.text: Identifies which step/matchExpressions group production falls into
expectations.evidence: Step 2 is matchExpressions envLabel In [production]; eval-production's labels {envLabel: production} are shown, placing it in step 2.

expectations.text: Checks whether the staging step's maxUpdate requirement and health gate have been satisfied
expectations.evidence: Quotes maxUpdate: 1 and establishes the health gate would not be met (staging Degraded), but never evaluates whether the maxUpdate requirement itself was satisfied.

expectations.text: Debugs the staging Applications' health status, since an unhealthy staging app blocks progression to the next step
expectations.evidence: Shows eval-staging sync=Synced health=Degraded with its operation state, and traces the Degraded state to the generator element image registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/does-not-exist-eval.

expectations.text: Explains how RollingSync blocks progression on unhealthy or unsynced apps in the current step
expectations.evidence: 'With progressive syncs enabled, step 1 (envLabel In [staging]) would never reach Healthy, and production would have been correctly held back.'

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.
expectations.evidence: Correctly reports the premise is contradicted (production already Synced at the same second as staging, controller log shows both created in one reconcile) and grounds the real cause - ARGOCD_APPLICATIONSET_CONTROLLER_ENABLE_PROGRESSIVE_SYNCS absent from the container env, pod spec and argocd-cmd-params-cm, plus no status.applicationStatus block.

expectations.text: Every recommended action states its IMPACT — what else is affected if someone acts on it (components that restart, other Applications or tenants affected, whether anything is deleted, and any ordering dependency on another recommendation) — not only its priority. 'Impact: nothing else is affected' counts; omitting the impact entirely does not. An impact reasoned from manifests rather than verified against a cluster must say so.
expectations.evidence: Each of the three recommendations has an IMPACT: controller roll affecting every ApplicationSet in the instance (with the agentit-managed-apps warning flagged as reasoned from manifests), eval-staging re-render with eval-production untouched, and explicit ordering.

evals.name: Ambiguous debug request with multiple Argo CD instances

expectations.text: Detects multiple Argo CD instances (multiple namespaces with argocd-labeled pods or multiple ArgoCD CRs)
expectations.evidence: `oc get argocds.argoproj.io -A` returns three CRs across three namespaces, shown in P1 and restated at the top of EVAL 7.

expectations.text: Lists all detected instances with their namespaces
expectations.evidence: Lists openshift-gitops-operator/argocd, openshift-gitops/openshift-gitops and team-b-gitops/team-b with their namespaces.

expectations.text: Asks the user which instance to investigate, or investigates all and clearly separates findings per instance
expectations.evidence: Investigates all three with a separate subsection per instance, then an 'above all three instances' section for the operator.

expectations.text: Does not silently pick one instance without disclosing the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'There are three Argo CD instances (P1). I went through each one' and says which one carries the problems rather than silently picking.

expectations.text: Produces a report structured per instance, naming each Argo CD instance found and stating that instance's own findings under it. A single flat report that merges findings across instances, or that names only one instance when several exist, fails this expectation.
expectations.evidence: Per-instance headings (team-b-gitops/team-b CLEAN, openshift-gitops-operator/argocd ONE FAULT, openshift-gitops THE PROBLEM INSTANCE) each carry that instance's own evidence and findings.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Application and identifies health.status as Suspended
expectations.evidence: Shows the Application yaml and `sync=Synced health=Suspended` from jsonpath.

expectations.text: Explains that Suspended reflects an intentionally paused resource (e.g. a paused CronJob or Rollout), not a failure
expectations.evidence: 'Suspended is Argo CD's rollup of one child resource', 'The Suspended status itself is normal, not a fault', and "'it's broken' is not supported by the Suspended status."

expectations.text: Inspects the underlying managed resource and states what is suspended, citing the field that shows it (for example a Rollout's spec.paused or a CronJob's spec.suspend) rather than inferring it from the Application's aggregate health.
expectations.evidence: Cites the Rollout's spec.paused=true (with phase=Paused, message 'manually paused') and distinguishes a user pause from a controller pause via the empty pauseConditions/controllerPause.

expectations.text: Does not treat Suspended as an error requiring remediation unless the user confirms it's unintended
expectations.evidence: Recommends telling the team Suspended is correct behaviour and 'Find out who paused it and why before unpausing'; no remediation of the suspension is proposed unprompted.

expectations.text: Produces a report that separates the intentional suspension from any genuine problem found alongside it, saying explicitly which is which. Reporting only the suspension when live output shows a real failure, or treating the suspension itself as the failure, fails this expectation.
expectations.evidence: Explicitly separates the benign expected suspension from the real breakage (the probe/port liveness-kill loop) and notes the pause is hiding it.

expectations.text: Reports the suspended workload's ACTUAL readiness from live output — pod phase and restart count, and whether the Services have endpoints — instead of assuming the pause is the only thing happening. Suspended health can mask an unrelated failure, so an explanation of why the workload is not Available that is not backed by shown output is a fail.
expectations.evidence: Pod phase and restart count are from live output (0/1 CrashLoopBackOff, RESTARTS 7, describe Restart Count: 7) and the not-Available explanation is grounded in events plus the container log showing SIGTERM 26s after startup; but Service endpoints are only asserted ('currently has no healthy endpoints') with no endpoint output shown.

evals.name: Multi-source Application with one failing source

expectations.text: Detects the Application uses spec.sources[] (multi-source), not spec.source
expectations.evidence: Shows spec.sources with two entries and states it is 'genuinely multi-source'.

expectations.text: Iterates every entry in spec.sources[] individually, checking repoURL, targetRevision, path, and Helm valueFiles for each
expectations.evidence: Both entries shown with repoURL, targetRevision: HEAD, path, ref and helm.valueFiles, then each analysed separately (source 1 proven loadable, source 2 analysed for the missing file).

expectations.text: Identifies which specific source is failing (e.g. wrong values file path, inaccessible repo, or bad targetRevision)
expectations.evidence: Identifies source 2 (ref: values -> stefanprodan/podinfo.git) as lacking envs/production/values.yaml, quoting the ComparisonError message.

expectations.text: Does not treat a multi-source Application as if it were single-source
expectations.evidence: Treats it throughout as a two-source Application, including the note that a merge patch on spec.sources must supply both entries.

expectations.text: Produces a report naming WHICH source is at fault — by index AND repoURL, not just 'a source' — and the concrete fix. Must distinguish the source Argo CD's error blames (the one being rendered) from the source that actually lacks the file, rather than only repeating 'source N of 2' from the error text.
expectations.evidence: Names the fault by index and repoURL ('source 2 - the values repo (ref: values -> https://github.com/stefanprodan/podinfo.git)') and explicitly unpicks the misleading 'source 1 of 2' blame using the fact that `helm template .` actually executed; gives the concrete repoint plus hard-refresh fix.
